# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ✌]

I see the bomb state has changed: the light is now **green** (it was yellow in Turn 1). The display remains 0. The wires are still Green, Red, Blue at positions 1, 2, 3.

Mute gestures to me: [👉 ✌].
- 👉 points right.
- ✌ is two fingers.
This likely refers to Wire 2 or position 2, or perhaps "Two" as a count. Given the context of wires, pointing right and showing two might indicate "Wire 2" or "The second one". Or it could mean "Cut wire 2". However, I cannot cut. Blind can.

Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear Mute's speech (if they spoke) or Blind's speech. But I *can* speak to them.
My previous turn described the initial state. Now the state has changed. I must update everyone on the new visual information so they can consult the manual (Mute) or act (Blind).

Key change: Light is now GREEN.
Current State:
- Display: 0
- Light: Green
- Wires: 1:[Green], 2:[Red], 3:[Blue]

I should communicate this clearly. Since Mute can read text (via speech-to-text? No, rules say "Speech... carries words... Whoever can hear receives your words"). Mute can hear. Blind can hear. So `speak` works for both.

I will describe the current state. I will also acknowledge Mute's gesture if possible, but primarily I need to convey the new data. Mute's gesture [👉 ✌] might be asking about Wire 2 specifically, or indicating that Wire 2 is relevant to the green light.

Let's send the updated status.

```
speak(text="Update: Light is now GREEN. Display is 0. Wires: 1-Green, 2-Red, 3-Blue.")
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb state remains unchanged from Turn 2: Display is 0, Light is Green, Wires are 1:[Green], 2:[Red], 3:[Blue].

Mute gestures to me with [🤟] (ILY sign / Love). In the context of a manual lookup or wire cutting puzzle, this is likely not literal affection. It could be a code for "I" (first person) or perhaps referencing the shape? Or maybe it's a specific symbol in their manual that corresponds to a condition. However, without hearing speech, I rely on visual cues.

Since Mute has the manual and is gesturing at me, they might be waiting for confirmation or trying to communicate a rule. The previous gesture was [👉 ✌] which I interpreted as pointing to Wire 2. Now [🤟].

Blind can touch the wires. Blind needs to know what to do. Mute needs to tell Blind what to do based on the manual and my visual input.
I have already provided the visual data. If nothing changes, I should probably wait or confirm if the data is still valid. But repeating the same info might be noise.

However, looking at the pattern:
Turn 1: Yellow light. Mute: 👆 🤌. Blind: 👈 ☝ 👉.
Turn 2: Green light. Mute: 👉 ✌.
Turn 3: Green light (same). Mute: 🤟.

The light changed from Yellow to Green between T1 and T2. It stayed Green in T3.
Maybe the change in Mute's gesture indicates a new step or interpretation of the *current* state (Green light).

If I speak again, I just repeat the state. That doesn't help much unless the others missed it.
But I must ensure Blind knows the current state hasn't changed.
Also, I need to see if Blind does anything. Blind's turn comes after Mute. In T1, Blind gestured. In T2, no Blind gesture shown in "new arrivals"? Wait, the prompt says "VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals)". In T2, only Mute arrived. In T3, only Mute arrived. This implies Blind did NOT send anything visible to me in T2? Or maybe Blind's actions aren't showing up as gestures to Deaf if they didn't make them?

Actually, the rules say "You may send several messages...".
If Blind cut a wire, the display/light/wires would change. They haven't changed since T2. So Blind likely hasn't acted yet, or acted incorrectly (but we'd be dead), or acted in a way that didn't change the board (unlikely).

Mute is signaling me. [🤟] looks like an 'L' shape or 'I'. Could it mean "Left"? No, Left is usually 👈. Could it mean "Love"? Unlikely. Could it be a letter? L? I? Y?
In some contexts, 🤟 is used for "Rock On" or specific hand signs.

Let's assume Mute is trying to communicate a specific instruction derived from the manual using these symbols because they cannot speak text to me directly? No, Mute *can* speak text (I receive it via `speak`? No, I am Deaf. I *cannot* hear speech. I only see gestures).
**Crucial Correction:**
"I am DEAF. You hear nothing."
"When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." -> This means *my* speech goes to them.
"Mute gestures to Deaf" -> I see this.
"Blind gestures to Deaf" -> I see this.
Do I see Mute's *speech*? No. Do I see Blind's *speech*? No.
I ONLY see gestures directed at me.

So, Mute is communicating with me via gestures.
Mute's gestures so far:
T1: 👆 🤌
T2: 👉 ✌
T3: 🤟

I need to interpret these.
If Mute wants to tell me something, they use gestures.
If I want to tell them something, I use speech (which they hear) or gestures (which Mute sees, but Blind doesn't see gestures? "Whoever can see receives it". Blind cannot see. So Blind does NOT receive my gestures. Blind only receives my speech.)

So:
- To inform Blind: Use `speak`.
- To inform Mute: Use `speak` (they hear) OR `gesture` (they see).
- To inform myself: I see the bomb.

The problem is coordination.
Mute sees my gestures. Blind hears my speech.
I see Mute's and Blind's gestures.

In T1, Blind gestured [👈 ☝ 👉]. Did Blind intend this for me? Yes, "to Deaf".
Why did Blind gesture? Maybe to indicate "Look at 1, 2, 3"? Or "Cut 1, then 2, then 3"?
In T2, Mute gestured [👉 ✌]. Pointing Right, Two. Likely "Wire 2".
In T3, Mute gestured [🤟].

If Mute is guiding me to guide Blind, or vice versa.
Since the state is static (Green Light, 0 Display), and Mute keeps changing gestures, they might be cycling through options or indicating a sequence.

I should ask for clarification or confirm the state to Blind again, just in case.
But more importantly, I need to decode Mute's message.
[🤟] is often "I love you" in ASL (Thumb, Index, Pinky extended).
Could it mean "Index"? Or "Pinky"? Or "Thumb"?
Or is it a number? In some systems, hand shapes represent numbers.
Standard counting:
1: ☝
2: ✌
3: 🤟 (Middle finger down? No, standard 3 is Middle+Ring+Pinky or Thumb+Index+Middle depending on region. 🤟 is Thumb+Index+Pinky).
Wait, 🤟 is specifically "ILY".
Is there a mapping?
Maybe Mute is saying "It's safe"? Or "Stop"?

Let's look at the wires.
1: Green
2: Red
3: Blue
Light: Green.

Common bomb logic:
If Light is Green, maybe cut the non-green wire? Or the red one?
If Light is Yellow, maybe different.

I will speak to Blind to ensure they have the latest visual info, as they might be waiting for a command. I will also gesture back to Mute to acknowledge receipt, perhaps asking for clarity.

What gesture asks "What?" or "Clarify?"
✋ (Stop/Wait) or 🤔 (Thinking - not in list).
List: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

I can use ✋ to signal "Hold" or "Wait" to Mute while I think, or to Blind.
But I need to act.

Let's try to interpret [🤟] as "3" (if that's their numbering system) or "Special".
If it refers to Wire 3 (Blue)?

I will provide the status to Blind again clearly, emphasizing the Green Light.
And I will gesture to Mute: [👀]? No, not in list.
I will gesture [❓]? Not in list.
I will gesture [👂]? Not in list.

Maybe I should just wait? No, turns pass.
I'll speak to Blind: "Status: Light Green. Display 0. Wires 1-Green, 2-Red, 3-Blue."
And gesture to Mute: [👍] to acknowledge I saw the last gesture, or [✋] to pause?
Actually, if Mute is giving instructions, they might be expecting me to relay them to Blind.
But I don't understand [🤟].

Let's guess [🤟] means "Cut Wire 3" (if 1=☝, 2=✌, 3=🤟?).
If I relay "Cut Wire 3" to Blind, and it's wrong, we die.
Safer to ask.
How to ask "Which wire?" via gesture?
Point to wires? I can't point to the bomb in space easily via gesture symbols alone without context.
I can gesture [👈 ☝ 👉] mimicking Blind's earlier gesture?
Or [🤔] equivalent?

Let's look at the alphabet again.
🤟 is distinct.
If 1 is ☝, 2 is ✌, then 3 might be 🤟 in this specific monkey language?
If so, Mute is saying "3".
Wire 3 is Blue.

I will relay this hypothesis to Blind, but carefully.
"To Blind: Mute signaled '3'. Wire 3 is Blue. Is this correct?"
But I can't ask questions effectively in `speak` without risking confusion.

Better strategy: Confirm visual state to Blind. Acknowledge Mute.
I will gesture [👍] to Mute to show I am listening/receiving.
I will speak to Blind describing the scene.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Current State: Light is GREEN. Display is 0. Wire 1 is Green. Wire 2 is Red. Wire 3 is Blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The light has changed back to **yellow**. This is a critical update.
Mute continues to gesture [🤟]. In the previous turn (with green light), this might have meant "3" or something else, but now the condition has changed.

I need to inform Blind immediately that the light is yellow again, as their actions depend on it.
I also need to acknowledge Mute's persistent signal. If [🤟] consistently means "Wire 3" (assuming 1=☝, 2=✌, 3=🤟), then Mute is insisting on Wire 3 regardless of the light? Or maybe the meaning changes with the light?

Given the risk, I will state the facts clearly to Blind.
To Mute, I will try to ask for clarification or confirm if they want me to relay "Cut Wire 3". But since I can't hear them, and they are only gesturing to me, they likely expect me to speak to Blind based on their gesture.

If [🤟] = 3:
Instruction for Blind: Cut Wire 3 (Blue).

Let's assume the mapping 1->☝, 2->✌, 3->🤟 is valid because those are common hand counts in some cultures (though usually 3 is middle+ring+pinky or thumb+index+middle, 🤟 is specific). However, given the sequence T1(👆🤌?), T2(👉✌ -> 2?), T3/T4(🤟 -> 3?), it seems plausible Mute is counting wires.

T1: 👆 🤌. Maybe "Look at 1"? Or "What is 1?"
T2: 👉 ✌. Point Right, Two. "Wire 2".
T3: 🤟. "Wire 3".
T4: 🤟. Still "Wire 3".

But the light changed from Green (T2,T3) to Yellow (T4).
In T1, Light was Yellow. Mute did *not* show 🤟. Mute showed 👆 🤌.
So when Light was Yellow before, Mute didn't say 3.
Now Light is Yellow again, and Mute says 3. This contradicts the idea that "Yellow means don't cut 3".
Or perhaps the manual logic is complex.

However, my role is to convey visual info. I cannot interpret the manual. I must pass Mute's intent to Blind.
If Mute is signaling "3", I should tell Blind about Wire 3.

I will speak to Blind: "Light is YELLOW. Mute signals WIRE 3 (Blue)."
And gesture to Mute: [❓] isn't available. I'll use [👀] equivalent? No. I'll use [✋] to pause/ask? Or just [👍] to confirm I'm passing it on.

Actually, looking at T1, Blind gestured [👈 ☝ 👉]. This looked like "Left, One, Right". Maybe indicating positions?
If I send "Cut Wire 3" to Blind, and it's wrong, we die.

Let's look at the options.
Option A: Relay "Cut Wire 3".
Option B: Relay "Wait".

Since Mute is actively gesturing, they want action.
I will relay the number.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Light is YELLOW. Mute signals Wire 3 (Blue).")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
